(a) adaptive routing and congestion can be stable, provided either the network traffic is fair or the routing algorithm is "well-behaved", and (b) adaptive routing and non-fair congestion control are unstable, even in simple networks.

(1) adaptive routing can yield stable optimal routing in the presence congestion control, provided the congestion control mechanism either (a) is fair or (b) that the network workload satisfies a reasonable stability constraint; (2) one or the other assumption (1a) or (1b) is necessary for this result to hold; and (3) we provide a simple algorithm for congestion control that meets the stability constraints of assumption (1b) above.
